loan-missing-due.whyObligationsCannotVanish: DueSettled requires exactly one retained identity. A missing due is not treated as already paid.

loan-erased-due.mutation: same as missing due: drop a retained record from supplied state
loan-erased-due.whyObligationsCannotVanish: Episode close and settlement change status to Settled without deleting the record. Erasing the record from the input is a mutation, not a legal transition.
loan-erased-due.citation: semantics.md obligation transition. semantics.test.mjs pop case.

loan-replayed-due.mutation: DueSettled against an already Settled tombstone
loan-replayed-due.whyObligationsCannotVanish: Tombstones retain identity for the genesis lifetime and reject a second settle.

loan-partial-due.mutation: raise retained outstanding above the emit amount so settle amount is below outstanding
loan-partial-due.citation: semantics.test.mjs amount 500000001 -> OBLIGATION_PARTIAL_UNSUPPORTED. semantics.md: amount below outstanding rejects this code.

loan-excess-due.mutation: lower retained outstanding below the emit amount

loan-duplicate-due.mutation: reset cursor and notional then accrue again while dues remain
loan-duplicate-due.whyObligationsCannotVanish: Tombstones and Outstanding records both occupy identity. Recreate is forbidden in this profile.
loan-duplicate-due.citation: semantics.test.mjs accrue after accrued with cursor/notional reset -> OBLIGATION_DUPLICATE

unresolvedCustody.statement: Pool outgoing effects are part of all-effects evidence. Principal debit caps alone do not prove pool or provider custody authorization. That external custody and consent relation remains an MC02, MC04, and MC05 obligation before public spending.
